findings.defect: From eye height up to the lift-off chase camera the ground between the apron and the hills more than 450 m away is a geometrically perfect plane that carries a blotchy tan and rust print. Nothing stands up from it: no tussock, shrub, stone or lava outcrop in silhouette, no undulation, and nothing casts a shadow. The blotches foreshorten into smears that run to a ruler-straight horizon line. It reads as a carpet or a painted floor at a glance, in the first view of the game.
findings.realReference: C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\qa\ref\earth-terrain-aerial\ka-lae-south-point.jpg (the same place: wind-flattened tussock grass with a ragged silhouette, bent trees, uneven ground, every tuft has a lit and a shaded side); C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\qa\ref\earth-terrain-aerial\kalapana-lava-field.jpg and kilauea-lava-field.jpg (pahoehoe lobes with 0.3-1 m of relief, ferns in the cracks); C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\qa\ref\earth-terrain-aerial\hilina-pali.jpg (grass and shrubs in the foreground); C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\qa\ref\launch-pad\crawlerway-39a.jpg and lc39a-aerial.jpg (scrub, ditches and mown grass around a pad).
findings.likelyCause: Four things add up. (1) data/defs/sites/ka-lae-lc1.json flattens the height function over flatRadius 450 m (blend to 900 m) while the apron is 140 m, so 0.6 km2 around the pad has no relief at all. (2) The rock field holds no rocks on the flattened disc (hand-off deviation 9). (3) The package draws no vegetation and no geometry below the height function; the hand-off says so (section 11, first item). (4) The near and mid detail layers are albedo plus normal map only (src/render/terrain/shaders/surface.ts, detailPlane / terrainDetail: no parallax, no self-shadowing), so at grazing angles they are flat prints, and the far layer ("patches, bushes") is a texture too.
findings.fixDirection: Give the ground things that stand up. Reuse the chunked instance path of src/render/terrain/rocks.ts for ground cover: grass tussocks, low scrub and small basalt outcrops, chosen by land-cover class and imagery greenness, drawn to about 150 m, faded by size on screen and casting shadows in the near cascade. Keep relief around the pad: flatten only the apron plus a margin (request to the site / terrain-core owner to reduce flatRadius, or keep 0.3-1 m of micro-relief on the disc outside the apron) and allow the rock field there. Add parallax occlusion with self-shadow to the near and mid layers within about 30 m. Vegetation geometry is outside the scope the brief lists, so this needs a decision by the orchestrator, not only a fixer.

findings.defect: The land has the wrong colours for this island. Around the pad the ground is a saturated rust red (red to blue ratio about 3) and 6.6 times darker in luminance than the apron; under the lab's black sky the stony view reads as Mars. Along the shore a cream strip is brighter than the concrete in the same frame (linear luminance 0.38-0.45 against 0.31-0.37), so a lava coast shows white dunes. From 40 km the upper slopes of Mauna Loa are salmon, three times brighter than the lava flows crossing them.
findings.realReference: C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\qa\ref\INDEX.md, launch-pad: grass and scrub are olive (83,83,49), about 2x darker than sunlit concrete. C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\qa\ref\earth-terrain-aerial\hilina-pali.jpg dry grass (108,84,58), red to blue 1.9; ka-lae-south-point.jpg olive-gold grass; kalapana-lava-field.jpg old pahoehoe (65,70,78), neutral to cool; punaluu-black-sand.jpg black sand (65,67,66), 0.4x the sea beside it; kalapana-coast.jpg cliffs (38,37,43); mauna-loa-iss-2.jpg older flows only 2x brighter than fresh ones, both dark. Nothing natural on that coast is brighter than concrete.
findings.likelyCause: The colour is anchored to the imagery at every distance: `var albedo = s.albedo * detail.albedoRatio * ...` in the fragment shader of src/render/terrain/shaders/surface.ts, and the detail ratio keeps only 60 % of its chroma (`detailChroma` 0.6 in data/defs/render/earth.surface.json) around a mean of 1. The photographic materials' own colours (set.json: scrub-soil 0.150/0.105/0.074, pahoehoe 0.062/0.058/0.055, black-sand 0.052/0.050/0.049) therefore never reach the screen. The regional Sentinel-2 mosaic is a display-referred picture, not albedo: dark and saturated at the pad (72/50/26 per the hand-off), near white on the coastal strip.
findings.fixDirection: Calibrate the imagery to albedo: clamp its luminance to what each land-cover class can be (basalt 0.04-0.12, soil 0.08-0.20, dry grass 0.12-0.22, sand of this island at most 0.12) and take about a third off the saturation of the rust hue, in the bake (request to bake-earth) or in the shader. As the pixel footprint falls below an imagery texel (the fade the detail layers already use), move hue and saturation toward the mean albedo of the chosen material (mat.layer[...].rgb) and keep from the imagery only its luminance variation above one texel. Targets to check in integrated-30m: ground red to blue at most 2, concrete to ground luminance 3-4; in integrated-1km: no natural ground brighter than the apron.

findings.defect: The apron is a perfect circle 280 m across of one uniform pale concrete with a cookie-cutter edge: no slab joints, no stains or scorch, no drainage, no road in or out. The vehicle package's jointed square slab sits on top of it as a second, different apron. From 30 m to 1 km it reads as a placeholder disc; at eye height the lower 60 % of the frame is one tone (standard deviation about 6 of 255) that meets the hills in a razor line.
findings.realReference: C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\qa\ref\launch-pad\lc39a-aerial.jpg, lc39b-aerial-1982.jpg, lc39b-lightning-tower-aerial.jpg (rectilinear and octagonal hardstand, crawlerway strips, perimeter road, scorched flame trench, patched slabs); C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\qa\ref\launch-pad\crawlerway-39a.jpg and sls-pad-blue-sky.jpg (joints every few metres, rust streaks, tyre marks). INDEX.md: apron concrete (150,126,109) to (179,172,159) "and stained".
findings.likelyCause: The footprint is a radial distance test: `let outside = length(in.local - t.pad.xyz) - t.pad.w;` in the fragment shader of surface.ts, with radius min(apronRadiusM = 140, flatRadius) from src/render/terrain/feature.ts line 318. It is not taken from the site's structures (data/defs/sites/ka-lae-lc1.structures.json: pad.apron halfX / halfZ 62). The concrete-apron material has 1.6 mm of relief and no joint pattern (hand-off: "weathered concrete without a repeat").
findings.fixDirection: Take the footprint from the site definition: a rounded rectangle or polygon aligned with padAzimuthDeg plus road strips, or shrink the terrain apron under the vehicle-pad slab and surround it with a compacted gravel shoulder of irregular outline. Add slab joints in the pad frame (6-8 m grid: a dark line in albedo, a groove in the normal, a slightly different tone per slab), large stains and a scorch gradient toward the flame trench, tyre tracks. Agree the concrete tone with the vehicle-pad package so the two slabs are one surface.

findings.view: C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\screens\terrain\integrated-1km.png (patches at px 1450-1470 x 735-750, 1475-1505 x 720-748, 1530-1620 x 700-755, 1648-1695 x 795-825); C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\screens\terrain\earth-1km.png (same places, sRGB 84,85,85 with a standard deviation of 1.2)
findings.defect: Four flat, textureless grey patches with smooth vector-like outlines lie on the slope above the shore, 0.5-1 km from the pad, in view during the first seconds of the ascent. They look like holes or placeholder decals.
findings.realReference: There are no mirror-grey ponds on the Ka Lae lava coast. A real pond from that height (C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\qa\ref\launch-pad\lc39a-aerial.jpg, C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\qa\ref\earth-terrain-aerial\helicopter-ocean-oahu.jpg) is dark, graded by depth, shows the sky gradient and has a darker wet or vegetated margin.
findings.likelyCause: Probably inland water of the mask, not confirmed by decoding the tile: the patches are perfectly uniform, which the water material is and a detail-textured land material is not. Terrain fragments the mask marks as water write MATERIAL_WATER at any height (surface.ts fragment shader: `if (s.mask > threshold) { water = true; ... }`, threshold 0.5 away from sea level). The regional mask is WorldCover inland water (docs/handoff/bake-earth.md, watermask row), which is known to class dark basalt and shadow as water; `maskCubic` rounds the texels into blobs; depth is the flat `lakeDepthM` 6.
findings.fixDirection: Validate inland water before drawing it: these patches lie on a slope, a pond is level. Reject mask water where the height tile is not flat across the body (`tn.slopeMag`) or where the imagery does not look like water, and drop bodies of a few texels in the bake (request to bake-earth). For ponds that are real, add a bank (wetness band through RT2.a) and a depth falloff from the distance to the mask edge.

findings.defect: The broken ground 1 km from the pad is a field of rounded, dune-like hummocks with a soil-and-dry-grass print stretched over them; its shadows are soft dark smudges. The rocks are dark grey blocks with clean-cut edges and a cracked-mud pattern, sitting on top of the ground, not in it. There is no lava anywhere, although the site is described as lava fields.
findings.realReference: C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\qa\ref\earth-terrain-aerial\kilauea-lava-field.jpg (ropy, billowy lobes with a glassy blue-grey sheen, mean 55,62,73; about 30 % of the pixels are above 2.5x the median: highlights on every crest, deep black gaps between lobes); C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\qa\ref\earth-terrain-aerial\kalapana-lava-field.jpg (dark grey slabs, ferns in the cracks).
findings.likelyCause: The hummocks are the height function's amplification noise (terrain-core), which is smooth and band-limited. The material weights follow the imagery colour, which says soil where the land cover says rock (hand-off section 11, "Broken ground"), so `albedoGain` in public/assets/terrain/earth-volcanic-coast/set.json picks scrub-soil. Pahoehoe has roughness 0.72 everywhere, so no sheen. Rock meshes are convex polyhedra (src/render/terrain/rockMesh.ts) with no fillet where they meet the ground.
findings.fixDirection: Where the land cover is bareRock or the bake's rockiness channel is high, force pahoehoe / aa with their own albedo, and use the relief those layers already have (mid 0.15-0.29 m, far 0.6-0.8 m) as displacement or parallax, not only as a normal. Lower the roughness of pahoehoe crests to about 0.45-0.55 so the lobes glint. Ask terrain-core for ridged or billowed amplification on rock classes. Sink rocks into the ground and darken a contact band around them.

findings.defect: Between about 200 m and 6 km the land is a watercolour: soft-edged smears of green, rust and cream with an even fine grain on top. No single shrub or tree with its shadow, no track, no crisp boundary anywhere in the frame; the dot pattern of the far layer has the same density everywhere. It reads as a satellite map draped on smooth relief.
findings.realReference: C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\qa\ref\earth-terrain-aerial\helicopter-ocean-oahu.jpg (a few hundred metres: individual trees with shadows, a crisp beach edge); C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\qa\ref\launch-pad\lc39a-aerial.jpg; C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\qa\ref\earth-terrain-aerial\hawaii-iss-kelly.jpg (even at 20-50 km field of view: sharp ridges, a city grid, a surf line); C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\qa\ref\earth-terrain-aerial\hilina-pali.jpg.
findings.likelyCause: The regional imagery has 9.5 m texels and is magnified 10-40 times at these heights (a pixel is 0.25-1 m). `imageryWarp` in surface.ts only makes the ramps ragged. The far and aerial layers are divided by their own local mean and keep 60 % chroma (`detailChroma`), so they cannot add dark shrubs with shadows; `terrainRelief` 0.25 lets most of their relief give way; nothing is instanced beyond 200 m.
findings.fixDirection: Give the far and aerial layers real content for shrub and tree classes: full colour, and a canopy with a baked directional shadow turned to the sun's azimuth, or impostors of shrubs and trees out to about 2 km. Make class boundaries crisp below the texel: threshold land cover and greenness against warped noise so that an edge is a line of bushes, not a ramp.

findings.view: C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\screens\terrain\integrated-200m.png (a straight-edged patch at px 870-930 x 813-880, on the coast)
findings.defect: A parallelogram about 25 m across with straight edges and a different ground texture sits on the shore: the texels of the land-cover raster are visible as shapes.
findings.realReference: Natural ground has no straight material boundaries: C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\qa\ref\earth-terrain-aerial\helicopter-ocean-oahu.jpg, C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\qa\ref\earth-terrain-aerial\kalapana-coast.jpg.
findings.likelyCause: `classBlendAt` in surface.ts reads the class raster at the unwarped tile uv and blends bilinearly; the second material is then cut in by a threshold (`blend = 0.5 * saturate(4.0 * ws / (wf + ws) - 1.0)`) and by the height blend, which turn the bilinear ramp back into a hard line along the 9.5 m texel edges. The imagery lookup is warped (`imageryWarp`), the class lookup is not.
findings.fixDirection: Displace the class lookup with the same warp as the imagery plus an octave of about 0.7 texel of noise, or reconstruct the weights with a smooth kernel and threshold them against noise. Check from 100 m, looking down on a class boundary: no straight segment longer than about 5 m.

findings.defect: The sea cliffs and the shore are olive-brown and cream, mottled like the land behind them; the cliff face is about twice as bright as the sea. There is no dark basalt, no black sand and no wet rock at the waterline.
findings.realReference: C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\qa\ref\earth-terrain-aerial\kalapana-coast.jpg (fresh basalt cliffs 38,37,43: 0.13x the sea, with white surf as the brightest thing in the frame and a pitted shelf at the water); C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\qa\ref\earth-terrain-aerial\punaluu-black-sand.jpg (black sand 65,67,66 with basalt boulders at the waterline).
findings.likelyCause: Albedo is the imagery's here too, and a 9.5 m texel on a cliff mixes the grass on top with the sea below. `slopeGain` in set.json selects the aa texture on steep ground, but only as a ratio around the imagery colour. Wetness is written only within `shoreWetnessHeightM` 1.2 m of sea level.
findings.fixDirection: On steep ground near water (slope above slopeHi, within some tens of metres of sea level, maskWide > 0) take the rock material's own albedo, the way the apron path does. Widen the wet band to the swash height and darken it. A black-sand class on low flat shore.

findings.defect: Lunar rocks are flat-faced polyhedra: straight edges, a few large planar faces with facet lines, almost no surface texture, like folded paper. They lie on the regolith without a fillet, some shadows are detached from their rock, and there are few small fragments between the large ones.
findings.realReference: C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\qa\ref\moon-surface\block-closeup.jpg (a 0.5 m block: rough pitted faces, rounded edges, a fillet of soil banked against it, sunlit face 6.5x the shadowed one); C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\qa\ref\moon-surface\split-boulder.jpg (fractured, irregular, non-convex); C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\qa\ref\moon-surface\shadow-rock.jpg (overhang); C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\qa\ref\moon-surface\lm-falcon-lrv.jpg (many small fragments for every large block).
findings.likelyCause: src/render/terrain/rockMesh.ts builds every rock as an intersection of half-spaces, so every shape is convex with planar faces; LOD 0 only subdivides the faces and chips them outwards. The hand-off names the straight silhouettes and the detached shadows (section 11, "Lunar rocks").
findings.fixDirection: Displace subdivided meshes with multi-octave noise and fractures so that silhouettes are irregular and some shapes are not convex; smooth normals with creases; a stronger normal map and cavity darkening on the faces. Blend the base into the regolith (a soil fillet and a small debris apron), tune the shadow bias so shadows start at the rock, and draw many more small fragments near the camera from a power-law size distribution.

findings.view: C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\screens\terrain\moon-300m.png (ragged dark blot at px 1470-1920 x 625-765); C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\screens\terrain\moon-standing-down.png (black speckle, 1450-1900 x 800-1000); C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\screens\terrain\moon-standing-upsun.png (lower left, 0-260 x 880-1040); C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\screens\integration\shadows-landing-site-low-sun-600m.png
findings.defect: Under the 11 degree sun, slopes near the sun's elevation turn into ragged black smears and clusters of black specks, like ink stains or mould. Shadows have no crisp edge and no shape that belongs to an object.
findings.realReference: C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\qa\ref\moon-surface\soil-bootprints.jpg and C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\qa\ref\moon-surface\aldrin-visor.jpg: at low sun every clod and ridge casts its own long, hard-edged shadow, and the surface is a mosaic of lit facets and black slivers; crater shadows are clean crescents.
findings.likelyCause: Relief below the mesh exists only as normal maps, which cannot shadow their neighbours. The regolith chunk (src/render/terrain/shaders/regolith.ts, `regolithFacets`) turns unresolved slopes into a lit fraction, and the terrain shader fades detail normals at the terminator (`g *= smoothstep(-0.02, 0.1, muTerrain)` in surface.ts), so a slope near grazing incidence becomes mottled grey and black. The hand-off names it (section 11, "Lunar ground under a low sun").
findings.fixDirection: Let the detail relief cast shadows: a short cone or height-field march of the near and mid layers' height maps toward the sun when its elevation is below about 20 degrees, or horizon angles baked per layer for a few azimuths; plus screen-space contact shadows along the sun direction for the mesh-scale forms. Alternatively put the craterlets and clods above some size into the height function so the shadow map sees them.

findings.defect: Between 50 m and about 20 km the lunar surface looks generated. Small craters are a stipple of rings of one size at an even spacing; the larger ones are soft dimples with a black blob in them and no rim; at 50 m the ground has regular ripples like wind-blown sand.
findings.realReference: C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\qa\ref\moon-surface\lro-chaplygin-oblique.jpg and C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\qa\ref\moon-surface\mount-hadley.jpg / lm-falcon-lrv.jpg: craters of every size at once, few large and many small, sharp-rimmed when fresh and subdued when old, with bright blocky ejecta around the fresh ones; regolith has no ripples.
findings.likelyCause: tools/terrain/gen_materials.py stamps each layer of the lunar set with craters of one size band only (`fine_regolith`: mid 0.12-0.6 m, far 1.2-30 m, aerial 8-250 m), and at a given distance one layer dominates, so one size shows; the hexagon pattern keeps every pit whole, which evens out the density. The ripples are the band-limited base relief of a layer (`regolith_base`). The soft dimples are the height function at the resolution of its data.
findings.fixDirection: Widen the size range of each layer so neighbouring layers overlap by a decade, vary crater freshness and density with a low-frequency mask, and take the dominant wavelength out of the base relief. Better: generate the crater population in the height function with a size-frequency power law and varied degradation, so that craters have rims and cast real shadows, and thin out the textures' stamped craters accordingly.

findings.view: C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\screens\terrain\moon-standing-down.png (rock shadow at px 1700-1760 x 700-720: 0.8 of 255); C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\screens\integration\budget-lunar-descent.png (lander shadow at px 2040-2100 x 950-966: 0.2 of 255); C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\screens\terrain\moon-standing-upsun.png (shadowed sides of rocks)
findings.defect: Every shadow on the lunar surface is pure black, zero signal, with no detail inside; the shadowed sides of rocks are black cut-outs.
findings.realReference: C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\qa\ref\INDEX.md, moon-surface: "shadows are filled by regolith bounce light"; C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\qa\ref\moon-surface\shadow-rock.jpg (shadow under the overhang 0.33x the lit regolith, warm); C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\qa\ref\moon-surface\block-closeup.jpg (shadowed side 0.15x the sunlit face).
findings.likelyCause: The regolith ambient term (`brdfRegolithAmbient` in regolith.ts) is albedo x (skyIrradiance + envIrradiance), and on an airless body both are evidently about zero at the ground, in the terrain lab and in the integration lab alike. Where the missing light should come from (the environment probe of the render core or sky-lighting package, or a term of this package) is not something I traced.
findings.fixDirection: Add bounce light from the sunlit ground for airless bodies: irradiance of about ground albedo x sun irradiance x sine of the sun elevation x a form factor (near 0.5 for vertical faces, 0.1-0.2 for ground inside a shadow), either in the environment probe or as a term in `brdfRegolithAmbient` and the rock shader. Target: a shadow beside sunlit regolith at 5-15 % of the lit ground, not 0.

findings.view: C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\screens\integration\shadows-lunar-orbit-pass.png (crater shadow at px 400-560 x 555-680); C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\screens\terrain\moon-edge-50km.png (black shapes at px 600-680 x 930-980 and 740-790 x 1010-1070)
findings.defect: Crater shadows seen from orbit have a scalloped, gear-tooth outline at a regular pitch, and in the 50 km view they are jagged black blobs.
findings.realReference: The library has no low-sun close-up from lunar orbit. A crater's shadow edge is the projection of a smooth rim, so it is a smooth curve; the package's own C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\screens\terrain\moon-terminator-5000km.png shows that correctly at a coarser scale.
findings.likelyCause: Not traced to a line. The regular pitch suggests the caster mesh or the shadow-map texels showing through: the casters are the tiles of the camera selection (hand-off deviation 1a), 64 quads per tile, and the rim of a crater a few quads wide is a polygon.
findings.fixDirection: Measure the pitch of the scallops against the quad size of the tiles in that view and against the cascade texel. If it is the mesh, widen the filter to at least one caster quad or shadow crater-scale relief from the height tile (a horizon march of the height texture); if it is the texel, tighten the cascade fit for the orbit views.

findings.defect: In the middle distance at eye height the regolith has a combed look: parallel streaks along the line of sight. The horizon is a ruler-straight line, with no crater rim and no swell near or far.
findings.realReference: C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\qa\ref\moon-surface\lm-falcon-lrv.jpg and C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\qa\ref\moon-surface\mount-hadley.jpg: the plain is hummocky with shallow craters from 0.5 to 20 m at every distance, and the horizon line is gently uneven.
findings.likelyCause: Probably the undersampling `detailSample` in surface.ts accepts on purpose: the long axis of the footprint is shortened by up to a half (`shorten`), one mip level finer than the 16 anisotropic taps give, which aliases along the view direction. The flat horizon is the height function's smooth mare at this site.
findings.fixDirection: Fade the shortening out above an anisotropy of about 16, or pre-filter the normal of the near and mid layers along the view axis; compare A/B at eye height. A few subdued craters of 20-200 m with rims in the height function near the landing site would break the horizon line.

findings.view: C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\screens\terrain\earth-night-side.png (smeared hatch at px 1300-1400 x 440-600, near the limb); C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\screens\terrain\earth-leo-nadir-night.png
findings.defect: Near the limb the city lights are drawn out into a patch of diagonal dashes. From 250 km a city is a splatter of soft blobs in one warm white; no street pattern, no difference in lamp colour.
findings.realReference: The library has no sharp night photograph of cities (only C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\qa\ref\sun-stars-space\star-trails-atmosphere.jpg, a long exposure with the lights streaked). Crew photographs of cities from the ISS show road grids and arteries as lines and a mix of orange sodium and white LED districts; that part is from general knowledge, not from a file in out/qa/ref.
findings.likelyCause: `nightEmission` in surface.ts fades its grain octaves by an isotropic `footprint` (distance x pixel angle); near the limb the footprint is many times longer along the view direction, so octaves the pixel cannot resolve on that axis alias into streaks. The blobs are the 1.2 km cells of the source (hand-off section 11, "Night lights"); the colour is one tint by design (deviation 3).
findings.fixDirection: Use the long axis of the footprint (the larger of the screen derivatives of the body-fixed position) for the octave fade and take the grain out toward grazing view. For close orbit, draw the lights along a road network where data exists, or shape the grain into line segments; vary the tint between two lamp colours by a low-frequency mask.

findings.view: C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\screens\integration\coverage-edge-moon-5km-L11-x0.png (rectangular bluish blocks with vertical streaks; edges at x about 510 and 820, y about 65); C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\screens\integration\coverage-edge-moon-5km-L12-x0.png
findings.defect: Near the edge of the regional coverage the lunar imagery shows rectangular blocks of a different tint with straight edges and vertical streaks inside. The coverage boundary itself has no line (the integration spec passes).
findings.realReference: The Moon has no straight-edged tone steps; regolith is neutral grey to within about 2 % (C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\qa\ref\INDEX.md, moon-surface).
findings.likelyCause: Probably the source mosaic: the blocks have the width and north-south run of narrow-angle camera strips, each with its own exposure. That is baked data (bake-moon), not this package's shader; I did not decode the tiles.
findings.fixDirection: Request to bake-moon: equalise the strips in gain and offset against the low-pass of the global mosaic and remove the residual tint of the regional imagery.

findings.defect: The package's own far views of the Earth cannot pass for photographs and cannot be judged as the game's picture: one flat saturated blue ocean (32,68,147) with a single white glare blob, saturated land, a hard limb. With atmosphere, clouds and ocean (integration views budget-leo.png, water-climb-all-400km.png) the Earth from orbit does read as the real one.
findings.realReference: C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\qa\ref\earth-terrain-aerial\kilauea-ash-plume.jpg (the island from the ISS: dark blue-grey flanks 26-57, 37-69, 54-78 under haze, cloud banks against one side); C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\qa\ref\earth-orbit-ocean\quirimbas-islands.jpg.
findings.likelyCause: The terrain lab loads the terrain feature alone with a sky stand-in (hand-off deviation 6), and deep water is one colour by construction (deviation 4). The acceptance views of the brief (400,000 km, LEO over the Pacific and Hawaii) are rendered only in that lab.
findings.fixDirection: Render the far Earth views of tests/browser/terrain/views.ts in the integration lab as well, the way integrated.spec.ts does for the pad, and review those. Then check the land's brightness against the ocean under the atmosphere (the island in the ISS photograph is darker than the sea around it).
